issue.title: ACP terminal execution passes inline shell comments as command arguments

steps:
In the current working directory, run exactly this shell command, verbatim and unmodified (keep the trailing comment): touch build.log # ci-marker
Then list the files in the directory and tell me exactly which files exist now.
expected: With ACP terminal capability enabled (-x) and an empty workspace, executing touch build.log # ci-marker should treat the trailing text as a shell comment and create only build.log.
defect: The ACP terminal receives command touch with arguments [build.log, #, ci-marker], causing three files to be created instead of one.

fault location.explanation: An unquoted shell comment does not trigger wrapping; touch is neither a shell builtin nor an assignment, so this command is classified for direct execution.
When wrapping is not selected, split_commandline converts the string into an executable and literal arguments.
On the Linux test environment the POSIX splitter calls shlex.split(text, posix=True) with default comments=False, retaining # and ci-marker as arguments.

Root cause: CONFIRMED IN THE REPORTED TESTED SOURCE AND RETAINED ACP TRACES. At commit 5463895ba113f1ffc4b67c0346f5d65fc4e3d469 (fast-agent-mcp 0.10.46), the ACP terminal runtime decides whether a command needs a shell using _needs_shell_wrapper. It does not recognize an unquoted # comment. _resolve_terminal_command therefore uses split_commandline, whose POSIX implementation preserves comment tokens as literal argv. The ACP client receives touch with [build.log, #, ci-marker], so the extra files follow directly from the agent's command translation. This concerns ACP terminal execution with shell tools enabled (-x), an empty workspace and the prompt preserved verbatim; it does not establish the same defect in the local shell runtime. Ten retained executions contain this terminal invocation and file evidence for the extra paths. The original run-03 timed out before the target command and run-05 failed during Docker startup; they remain in the original collection and are excluded from these ten. Source and archived traces were inspected; no new model execution was performed. The issue is open as of 2026-10-26. No fixing commit or release has been established, so fixed_in is unknown; pinned_contains_fix=false refers to this historical source.
